fields.label: Intro
paragraphs: These are pressure-energised sections: the medium pushes the lip against the sealing surface, so the seal grips harder as pressure rises and runs light when it falls. Which section suits depends on the pressure, whether the duty is single or double acting, and how much clearance the housing leaves.

fields.label: Cards ×6
rows: A cup-section seal on a plunger, sealing on its outside diameter against the bore. Single acting, tolerant of a less precise bore than a U-cup, and the section that has been in service longest.
Dosing and metering pumps, sprayers, hand and foot pumps
A U-section lip seal for a rod or a piston, single acting. The lip is energised by pressure and relaxed without it, so it runs cooler and drags less than a squeezed section.
Low and medium-pressure cylinders, pump rods
Seals on the rod, keeping the medium inside the cylinder. Sized to the rod diameter, the groove and the clearance — housings to ISO 5597 where the design follows the standard.
Seals on the bore, keeping pressure on one side of the piston. Single acting to ISO 6547, or paired back to back for double acting.
Stacked V-rings between a male and a female adaptor, adjustable by the gland. The set is tightened as it wears rather than replaced, which suits plant that cannot be stripped often.
Plunger pumps, valve stems, high-wear duty

Keep dirt, dust and moisture off the rod on the return stroke. Not pressure seals — they protect the rod seal behind them, and they are the cheapest part in the assembly to renew. Housings to ISO 6195.
Any rod running in a dirty environment
fields.note:
The wipers card is the honest one. A wiper is not a seal and saying so — “not pressure seals, they protect the rod seal behind them” — prevents the specification error where a buyer fits a wiper and wonders why it leaks.
Plunger cups lead the six because Margo already makes them. Sheet SKU 31 is a plunger cup page and it is the only reciprocating seal in the catalogue today. Everything else in this section is a capability statement, and the card order says which is which without announcing it.
Three ISO housing standards are named — 5597, 6547, 6195. They are dimensional standards for the housing, not product approvals, and section 07 states that distinction the way the oil-seal sheets do for DIN 3760

sections.title: Surface finish and the clearance gap
sections.live: NO LIVE SECTION → accordion, two panels, from the /products/bellows component

fields.label: H2
lines: Most Reciprocating Seals Fail on the Housing, Not the Seal
fields.value: Most Reciprocating Seals Fail on the Housing, Not the Seal
fields.note: 10 words · the strongest heading on this page. It is true, it is counter-intuitive, and it reframes the enquiry from “which seal do I buy” to “is my housing right” — a conversation only a supplier who has debugged these can have

fields.label: Panel 1 — Surface finish
paragraphs: A reciprocating seal needs a thin film of the medium under the lip to survive, and the rod finish is what holds it. Too rough and the surface abrades the lip; too smooth and there is nothing for the film to sit in, so the lip runs dry and glazes. Ra 0.1 to 0.4 µm is the usual window for a hard chrome-plated rod. Tell us the finish and the plating — if the rod is ground rather than plated, or has been polished during a rebuild, that changes our recommendation more than the compound does.
leads: Too rough and the surface abrades the lip; too smooth and there is nothing for the film to sit in, so the lip runs dry and glazes.
marked: A reciprocating seal needs a thin film of the medium under the lip to survive, and the rod finish is what holds it. **Too rough and the surface abrades the lip; too smooth and there is nothing for the film to sit in, so the lip runs dry and glazes.** Ra 0.1 to 0.4 µm is the usual window for a hard chrome-plated rod. Tell us the finish and the plating — if the rod is ground rather than plated, or has been polished during a rebuild, that changes our recommendation more than the compound does.
fields.note: 94 words · the extractable answer for this page. “Too smooth is as bad as too rough” is genuinely surprising to most buyers and it is correct. The rebuild-polishing detail is the kind of specific that only comes from having seen the failure — a rebuilt cylinder with a mirror rod eats seals, and nobody warns the maintenance team

fields.label: Panel 2 — Extrusion and the clearance gap
paragraphs: Under pressure a rubber section is pushed towards the clearance between rod and housing. If the gap is too wide for the pressure and the hardness, the seal extrudes into it and the extruded edge is nibbled away on every stroke — the classic bitten-lip failure. Three things fix it and they trade against each other: close the gap, raise the hardness, or fit a back-up ring behind the seal. That is why we ask for the clearance and the pressure together, and why a harder compound is sometimes the answer to a leak rather than a softer one.

sections.title: Technical & commercial questions
sections.live: NO LIVE SECTION → FAQ accordion, six questions · these six are the FAQPage mainEntity, verbatim

fields.label: Q1

lines: What is the difference between an oil seal and a reciprocating seal?

parts.text: Motion. An oil seal is designed for a rotating shaft — it has a garter spring holding the lip against the shaft, and the lip is shaped to pump fluid back as the shaft turns. A reciprocating seal works a stroke: no garter spring, a section that is energised by pressure rather than by a spring, and a lip that has to survive being dragged along the rod. Fitting one where the other belongs is the most common specification error we see. Rotary duty is on our oil seals page; this page is reciprocating.
parts.lead: Rotary duty is on our oil seals page; this page is reciprocating.

fields.note: 92 words · the extractable answer and the anti-cannibalisation answer at the same time. It wins a real informational query, it corrects the error the whole page exists to correct, and its last sentence routes rotary intent to /products/oil-seals from inside the FAQ schema

fields.label: Q2

lines: My seal is leaking after a few weeks. What is wrong?

parts.text: Usually the housing rather than the seal. Look at the failed part: a glazed, hardened lip means heat or a rod too smooth to carry a lubricating film; a lip nibbled along one edge means it is extruding into the clearance gap under pressure; scoring across the lip means the rod is too rough, or the wiper in front of it has failed and is letting grit through. Send us the part and the rod finish and we will tell you which of the three you have.

fields.note: 88 words · the highest-intent question in this category and the one that converts a maintenance engineer holding a failed part. Three failures, three causes, each identifiable by eye — and the answer ends in an offer rather than a product

fields.label: Q3

lines: Do you work to ISO 5597 and ISO 6195 housings?

parts.text: Yes. Where your design follows the standard we mould to the standard groove; where it does not, we mould to your drawing. These are dimensional standards for the housing, not certifications, and we hold no product approval against them — send the groove dimensions either way and we will confirm the section.

fields.note: 52 words · answers a qualifying question and closes the standards-as-credentials door in the same breath. The phrasing mirrors sheet SKU 14 on DIN 3760, which is the house position on dimensional standards

fields.label: Q4

lines: Can you supply polyurethane hydraulic seals?

parts.text: No. Polyurethane is the usual material for high-pressure hydraulic rod and piston seals and we do not mould it — we compound and mould vulcanised rubber, in eight compounds. Our reciprocating seals suit pump, sprayer, dosing and lower-pressure cylinder duty. If your specification calls for polyurethane we will say so rather than substitute a nitrile section that will not hold the pressure.

fields.note: 62 words · the refusal that makes the page trustworthy, and the third page in this run to decline work by naming a material Margo does not mix — polyurethane on mining and lining, butyl on lining, polyurethane again here. Substituting a nitrile section into a polyurethane application is exactly the failure this answer prevents, and it would be an easy sale to make

fields.label: Q5

lines: What is the minimum order quantity for seals?

parts.text: We supply in bulk. The minimum run is 10,000 pieces per part number, per compound, or quoted against the part where geometry or tooling makes that unrealistic. Prototype and first-article lots sit outside the minimum.

fields.note: 36 words · the standard answer, client-instructed 2026-09-01, unchanged. Do not reword it

fields.label: Q6

lines: What are your payment and delivery terms for international orders?

parts.text: TT and LC accepted, discussed per order. Ex-works Nashik or FOB Nhava Sheva. Commercial invoice, packing list and certificate of origin are issued with every consignment. Seals are packed to protect the sealing lip.
